articles.summary:
Animal that menaced residents was shot in October but then reappeared – and was shot for a second time and killed

A coyote that California wildlife officials believed they had euthanized after it bit a toddler and menaced residential pets in a trendy Los Angeles neighborhood was seen alive recently, neighborhood residents said.

Wiley, the name some Atwater Village residents gave to the coyote, had vexed the area with its increasingly aggressive and brazen behavior. The wild animal, which scampered through people’s backyards, was reportedly being fed by an unidentified man. Wiley’s presence drew local uproar after he bit a 16-month-old child.

articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom unseats Cindy Hyde-Smith in stunning Mississippi Senate win
articles.summary:
Colom takes victory by razor-thin margin in state that has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982

Democrat Scott Colom defeated Cindy Hyde-Smith, the incumbent Republican senator, to become the first Black senator in Mississippi elected since Reconstruction, in a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states.

“All I did was have the courage to imagine a night like this,” Colom told a crowd of hundreds who on Wednesday had gathered at Tougaloo College for his victory party. “I had the courage to believe in Mississippi. I had the courage to understand that we can show the country that Mississippi matters.”

Continue reading...

articles.title: Democrats push to rein in Trump on immigration after voter backlash to ICE raids
articles.summary:
Members of Congress seek to ‘bring sanity’ to system but decline to give details on plans to reform or abolish agency

A group of congressional Democrats on Wednesday pushed for immediate efforts to rein in the Trump administration’s sweeping immigration enforcement operation and “bring sanity” to an immigration system that Donald Trump said, after his party’s midterm drubbing, had been “too tough” in certain aspects.

Just over a week after the midterm elections in which the US president’s harsh crackdown on immigration fueled a voter backlash against Republicans, some sitting and newly elected Democrats gathered outside the US Capitol in Washington to advocate for a bipartisan approach to reforms – even as they gear up to take control of both legislative chambers next year.
